newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM AIMS TO SAVE NLG 1.5 BLN IN THREE YEARS.
newsitem.headline: KLM AIMS TO SAVE NLG 1.5 BLN IN THREE YEARS.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Tuesday it planned savings of at least 1.5 billion guilders over the next three years in order to improve profits.
KLM said it had initiated a "sweeping process of change" to bring about a "substantial improvement in profits".
"KLM considers a turnaround in its results of at least 1.5 billion guilders over a three-year period is required to achieve the desired profitability goals," it said in a statement.
The planned improvement in results will be achieved by reducing costs and raising revenues, it added.
KLM said it was implementing the new "Focus 2000" programme because measures implemented since 1991 were no longer able to deliver further improvements in productivity and unit costs.
The Dutch flag carrier said it would continue to aim for a 14 percent return on equity.
"In view of the current capital ratios this requires an operating result of approximately 800 million guilders," it said.
KLM chairman Pieter Bouw told reporters that to achieve this KLM would need to raise its operating profits by at least 1.5 billion guilders over a three-year period.
"About a third of this improvement must be derived from revenues and two-thirds from cost-reductions," he said.
This corresponded to a reduction of some 20 percent in the unit costs that fell within KLM's control, he added.
Bouw said KLM would review its route network, withdrawing from less profitable routes and redeploying capacity to more profitable ones.
KLM would strip its services of elements which did not help to improve margins and would examine opportunities to outsource and spin off support services, he said.
Bouw said KLM would also examine how its cargo division could raise its contribution to the airline's overall profit more quickly, he added.
